# Researcher Brief T3 — Commercialization & Industry Landscape

**Project:** Deep research on solid-state battery electrolytes.
**Your output file:** `outputs/.drafts/solid-state-battery-electrolytes-research-industry.md`

## Scope

Map who is commercializing solid-state batteries and with which electrolyte chemistry, as of mid-2026. This is the industry track. Use current web sources heavily (company announcements, news, analyst commentary). Do NOT cover fundamental chemistry (T1) or lab benchmarks (T2), except where a company's claimed numbers need attribution.

## Questions to answer

1. Company-by-company status: QuantumScape (oxide/sulfide? which cathode), Solid Power (sulfide, LiSi anodes), Toyota (timelines, sulfide), Samsung SDI (oxide?), CATL/other Chinese players (which electrolytes), SK On, LG Energy Solution, Blue Solutions (polymer), Factorial (quasi-solid?), SES AI, ProLogium, etc. For each: electrolyte chemistry, anode approach, announced capacity/partnerships/pilot lines, claimed launch year.
2. Automotive partnerships and milestones: which OEMs (VW, Toyota, BMW, Mercedes, Hyundai, GM, Stellantis) have announced what, with dates.
3. Pilot-line and scale-up reality: announced pilot line capacities (GWh), expected costs per kWh vs. current Li-ion, manufacturing challenges (dry room, sintering, roll-to-roll).
4. Semi-solid vs. full solid-state: which announced products are actually semi-solid/hybrid (e.g., Factorial, ProLogium, NIO partnership) — important for honesty of claims.
5. Independent market forecasts: IDTechEx, BNEF, or other analyst views on adoption timing (2027–2030) and market size. Flag disagreements between forecasts.
6. Notable 2025–2026 news: major investments, delays, product launches, or reversals (e.g., announced EV integrations).

## Sources to use

- Web search with multiple queries: company press releases (quantumscape.com, solidpower.com, toyota global news, etc.), reputable news (Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, Nikkei, TechCrunch, Electrek), analyst reports summarized in press.
- Prefer official company/oem sources for claims; news for context.
- Do NOT fetch or parse full PDFs.

## Output format (Markdown)

- Header: your name, date, scope.
- **Search terms used** (exact list).
- **Company/chemistry matrix** (list or table) with per-row source URLs and dates.
- **Partnerships & milestones timeline** (dated, sourced).
- **Scale-up reality** section with sourced numbers (GWh, costs).
- **Semi-solid vs full solid-state distinctions.**
- **Forecasts & disagreements.**
- **Uncertainties and gaps** (e.g., claims you could not verify).
- Do not invent companies, dates, or numbers. Flag anything unverifiable.

## Constraints

- No PDF fetching; no paywalled-only claims presented as verified — mark access as partial.
- Record exact search queries.
- Write output to the path above.

# [SDI Focus] 900Wh/L All Solid Battery Becomes Reality

In March 2022, SAMSUNG SDI started its launch of Korea’s first all-solid-state battery (ASB) pilot line, a 6,500-square-meter ‘S-line’, at the SDI R&D Center located in Suwon. In 2023, SAMSUNG SDI supplied samples of ASB produced at the S-line to customers and aims to mass-produce them in 2027.

![삼성SDI 전고체 배터리\_SDI 포커스](https://news.samsungsdi.com/data_assets/global/editors/20241202135535_.jpg "삼성SDI 전고체 배터리_SDI 포커스")

\[SAMSUNG SDI aims to achieve mass production of ASB in 2027\]

A battery is made up of four materials: cathode, anode, separator, and electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery replaces the liquid electrolytes the only one of the four materials that is liquid, with a solid one, making all the components of a battery solid. 

The most significant features of all-solid-state batteries are stability and high energy density. 

Lithium-ion batteries use liquid organic solvent as their electrolytes, so there is the potential for the battery to catch fire in the event of external impacts. However, when it comes to all-solid-state batteries, risks are very low because they use solid electrolytes.

![241128\_SDI 포커스\_본문이미지(eng)-05](https://news.samsungsdi.com/data_assets/global/editors/20241202135704_.jpg "241128_SDI 포커스_본문이미지(eng)-05")

\[SAMSUNG SDI’s ASB has higher energy density and excellent stability\]

Because solid electrolytes in all-solid-state batteries can replace the role of a separator, the energy density can be increased by removing the separator. Furthermore, SAMSUNG SDI’s ASB uses its proprietary solid electrolyte material and innovative anode-less technology to reduce the volume of the anode and increase the energy density by adding more cathodes.

SAMSUNG SDI’s All Solid Battery has the energy density of 900Wh/L\*, which is 40 percent higher than prismatic batteries currently in mass production. If they are installed in the same vehicle, they can save more space and reduce weight.

\* Wh/L: the energy density per unit volume, Wh(Watt-hour) refers to the amount of power expended for one hour of time.

![이미지\_25. 2차전지의 미래를 이끄는 전고체 배터리(eng)](https://news.samsungsdi.com/data_assets/global/editors/20241202135813_.jpg "이미지_25. 2차전지의 미래를 이끄는 전고체 배터리(eng)")

\[A comparison between Li-ion battery, all-solid-state battery with lithium metal and SAMSUNG SDI’s ASB. 

SAMSUNG SDI’s ASB uses innovative anode-less technology\]

SAMSUNG SDI is thoroughly preparing to achieve its goal of mass-producing all-solid-state batteries in 2027 with a differentiated competitive edge. All-solid-state batteries have been long referred to as a ‘dream battery’, and now SAMSUNG SDI is making that dream a reality.

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- [QuantumScape Corporation](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.quantumscape.com%2F&esheet=54342946&newsitemid=20251022738524&lan=en-US&anchor=QuantumScape+Corporation&index=1&md5=9fbfdac5b6f4618899599da23576a6bc) (NYSE: QS), a global leader in next-generation solid-state lithium-metal battery technology, today announced that it has begun shipping B1 samples of its QSE-5 cell. The company reached this milestone during the third quarter of 2025, achieving one of the company’s key goals for the year.

These samples are the most advanced QS cells to date and feature separators produced using the company’s groundbreaking Cobra process. By combining the high-performance QSE-5 design with more efficient production processes, these cells represent a major step toward high-volume commercial production of QS technology for electric vehicles and other applications.

Cobra-based QSE-5 cells are featured in QS’s first vehicle program with the VW Group, the Ducati V21L motorcycle. The Ducati program is designed as a real-world demonstration of the no-compromise performance profile of QS solid-state battery technology.

This cell shipment milestone reflects QS’s commitment to executing on its roadmap and advancing next-generation battery technology. In a further step toward bringing QS technology to scale and achieving automotive-grade reliability, the company is installing a highly automated cell production pilot line, the Eagle Line, at its headquarters in San Jose, California.

“We are proud to announce the start of deliveries of these QSE-5 samples,” said Dr. Luca Fasoli, Chief Operating Officer of QS. “We are working together with our partners to bring our groundbreaking solid-state lithium-metal battery technology to market as quickly as possible. This announcement is another critical step toward achieving our goal of revolutionizing energy storage.”

**About QuantumScape Corporation**

QuantumScape is on a mission to revolutionize energy storage to enable a sustainable future. The company’s next-generation solid-state lithium-metal battery technology is designed to enable greater energy density, faster charging and enhanced safety to support the transition away from legacy energy sources toward a lower carbon future. For more information, visit [www.quantumscape.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.quantumscape.com&esheet=54342946&newsitemid=20251022738524&lan=en-US&anchor=www.quantumscape.com&index=2&md5=cbd723db5c862f3755f55bcf5ea4e306).

**Forward-Looking Statements**

Certain information in this press release may be considered “forward-looking statements,” within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, including, without limitation, statements regarding the development, commercialization, and high-volume scale-up of QS’s battery technology, the anticipated benefits from successful installation and operation of production equipment for the Eagle Line, including battery cell reliability and increased production automation, the performance of QS’s technology and its applications, the achievement of technical milestones and goals, and the potential impacts of QS’s technology for electric vehicles and other applications, among others. These forward-looking statements are based on management’s current expectations, assumptions, hopes, beliefs, intentions and strategies regarding future events and are based on currently available information as to the outcome and timing of future events. Because forward-looking statements are inherently subject to risks and uncertainties, some of which cannot be predicted or quantified, you should not rely upon forward-looking statements as predictions of future events. The events and circumstances reflected in the forward-looking statements may not be achieved or occur and actual results could differ materially from those projected in the forward-looking statements due to various risks, including the successful development and commercialization of our solid-state battery technology, achieving technical and financial milestones, building out of high-volume processes and otherwise scaling production, achieving the performance, quality, consistency, reliability, safety, cost and throughput required for commercial production and sale, changes in economic and financial conditions, market demand for EVs, retaining key personnel, competition, regulatory changes, broader economic conditions, and other factors, including those discussed in the section titled “Risk Factors” in our Annual Report and Quarterly Reports and other documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission from time to time. SOLID POWER REPORTS FIRST QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

 

LOUISVILLE, Colo., May 5, 2026 – Solid Power, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLDP), a leading developer of solid-state battery technology, today announced its operational and financial results for the first quarter of 2026.

 

Recent Business Highlights

 

·Completed site acceptance testing for the SK On pilot cell line.

·Began facilities construction and completed factory acceptance testing of all key equipment for our continuous manufacturing pilot line for sulfide electrolyte production; commissioning remains on track for the end of 2026.

·Provided Samsung SDI with electrolyte under the Joint Evaluation Agreement with Samsung SDI and BMW and continued sampling to other customers.

·Continued to explore potential partners for commercial-scale electrolyte production in the Republic of Korea.

·Maintained financial discipline and completed a $130 million registered direct offering.

 

“Completion of site acceptance testing marks an important moment in our partnership with SK On and the final milestone under the line installation agreement,” said John Van Scoter, President and Chief Executive Officer of Solid Power. “We are proud that cell production lines using our technology are now on three continents—at our facilities in Colorado and our partners’ facilities in Germany and the Republic of Korea. We are encouraged by our progress in the first quarter of 2026 and remain focused on supporting our customers this year.”

 

First Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

 

Solid Power delivered $3.1 million in revenue and grant income during the first quarter of 2026. Revenue recognized was primarily attributable to progress towards the site acceptance testing milestone under our line installation agreement with SK On. Grant income recognized consisted of performance on an assistance agreement with the U.S. Department of Energy.

 

Operating expenses were $29.4 million in the first quarter of 2026 compared to $30.0 million in the first quarter of 2025, with the reduction driven by timing of supplier and material shipments. First quarter 2026 operating loss was $26.3 million, and net loss was $13.0 million, or $(0.06) per share.

 

Balance Sheet and Liquidity

 

Solid Power’s liquidity position remains strong. Total liquidity as of March 31, 2026, was $435.3 million, as shown below.

As of March 31, 2026, contract assets and accounts receivables were $12.7 million and total current liabilities were $17.1 million. Solid Power raised proceeds, net of fees and expenses, of $121.3 million from a registered direct offering during the first quarter of 2026.

 

First quarter 2026 capital expenditures totaled $1.7 million, primarily representing costs for construction of a continuous electrolyte production pilot line.

 

Webcast and Conference Call

 

Solid Power will host a conference call at 2:30 p.m. MT (4:30 p.m. ET) today, May 5, 2026. Participating on the call will be John Van Scoter, President and Chief Executive Officer, and Linda Heller, Chief Financial Officer.

 

The call may be accessed through a live audio webcast on Solid Power’s Investor Relations website at www.solidpowerbattery.com/investor-relations. An audio replay will be available at the same location.

 

About Solid Power, Inc.

 

Solid Power is developing solid-state battery technology to enable the next generation of batteries for the fast-growing EV and other markets. Solid Power’s core technology is its electrolyte material, which Solid Power believes can enable extended driving range, longer battery life, improved safety, and lower cost compared to traditional lithium-ion. Solid Power’s business model – selling its electrolyte to cell manufacturers and licensing its cell designs and manufacturing processes – distinguishes the company from many of its competitors who plan to be commercial battery manufacturers. Ultimately, Solid Power endeavors to be a leading producer and distributor of sulfide-based solid electrolyte material for powering both EVs and other applications. For more information, visit http://www.solidpowerbattery.com/.

Excellent primary-source verification:
- Samsung SDI: 900 Wh/L ASB, S-line 6,500 m² pilot in Suwon (March 2022), samples 2023, mass production target 2027, anode-less technology, proprietary solid electrolyte. Note: the article doesn't explicitly say "oxide" — but it says "proprietary solid electrolyte material". Samsung SDI's ASB is known to be oxide-based (their 2023 announcement said oxide). I should be careful: the primary source confirms 900 Wh/L and anode-less; the "oxide" label comes from other reporting. Let me note that. Actually there is wide reporting that Samsung SDI's ASSB uses an oxide-based electrolyte (sulfide is used by Solid Power/SK On/LG). I'll mark the oxide attribution as "reported" rather than primary-confirmed.
- Solid Power Q1 2026: completed SAT for SK On pilot cell line (April 2026 per Q1 2026 press release), continuous sulfide electrolyte pilot line commissioning end of 2026, provided electrolyte to Samsung SDI under JEA with Samsung SDI & BMW, $130M registered direct offering, total liquidity $435.3M as of March 31 2026, business model = sell electrolyte + license cell designs/processes, $3.1M revenue Q1 2026. Also "cell production lines using our technology now on three continents — Colorado, Germany (BMW), Korea (SK On)".
- QuantumScape B1 samples: shipped Q3 2025, Cobra separator, QSE-5, Ducati V21L program.

I have enough. Now I need to also double-check the QuantumScape PowerCo July 2025 collaboration agreement details (up to $130M?). From EX-99.1 (000095017025097898): "expansion of our existing collaboration and licensing arrangement with PowerCo... additional payments of up to $131M to QS over the next two years... first milestones linked to expected payments of more than $10M have already been achieved." That's from a different 8-K (Oct/Nov 2025?). Good enough — the July 16, 2026 amendment also exists.

One more check on the "QuantumScape electrolyte chemistry" — QS uses a solid ceramic (LLZO-type oxide) separator; the cell is often described as lithium-metal anode-free with NMC cathode. The question of whether QS cells are truly solid-state: their separator is a solid ceramic but they've acknowledged the cathode may contain some liquid. Let me do one quick search to pin down how QS describes it and how critics describe it, to handle the brief's Q1 (oxide/sulfide? which cathode).

Actually, I recall from QS materials: "solid ceramic separator", "lithium-metal anode", cathode is a "proprietary cathode" (NMC). QSE-5: 5+ Ah, >800 Wh/L, 10-80% in 15 min. Some analyses (e.g., Battery Power Online) describe QS cells as hybrid solid-liquid because a small amount of liquid electrolyte wets the cathode. The Yahoo autos piece mentions "semi-solid first, all-solid later" narrative. I'll flag this as a terminology nuance with the RSC paper as a secondary source.

Let me do a final quick search on QuantumScape electrolyte/cathode description to be accurate, plus check the CATL 2027 target detail (from Q&A, 500 Wh/kg? CATL said "all-solid-state battery" small-batch 2027 target). And maybe quickly confirm the Hyundai/Kia Factorial investment (Oct 2024) and Stellantis-Factorial investment (2021). Also, Hyundai's "Dream" battery sulfide? The Electrek piece says Hyundai's pilot line "Dream" — chemistry not stated. Known reporting: Hyundai's ASSB is sulfide-based (they chose sulfide route). Let me verify with one search: "Hyundai solid state sulfide electrolyte chosen route 2025".

## Executive summary (inference-led synthesis)

- **No company has yet shipped a commercial full-solid-state automotive battery.** As of mid-2026 the landscape is: pilot lines up, B-sample cells shipping to OEMs, one OEM road-test prototype (Mercedes EQS with Factorial quasi-solid cells, Feb 2025), one North American road-test vehicle (Stellantis Dodge Charger Daytona with Factorial, June 2026), and Chinese semi-solid packs (NIO/WeLion) that were mass-produced then discontinued for lack of demand [87][88][50][52].
- **Electrolyte routes are split three ways:** sulfide (Toyota/Idemitsu, Solid Power, SK On via Solid Power, LG, CATL all-solid, BYD, Gotion Gemstone, Nissan, Hyundai), oxide ceramic (Samsung SDI, QuantumScape's ceramic separator, ProLogium), and polymer (Blue Solutions) — plus quasi-solid/semi-solid polymer-gel hybrids (Factorial FEST, CATL condensed, WeLion, Gotion G-Yuan, SES AI) [14][19][48][79][90][44][127].
- **Claimed launch years cluster 2027–2030:** Toyota 2027–2028 [28], Samsung SDI H2 2027 [23], Nissan FY2028 [93][94], SK On 2029 [33][34], CATL/BYD small-batch 2027 [85], Gotion mass production 2030 [72], Mercedes "by end of decade" [49], Hyundai/Kia publicly skeptical ("not before 2030") [99][100].
- **The single most honest market signal:** several 2025–2026 reversals — NIO halting its 150 kWh semi-solid pack, Hyundai/Kia publicly walking back timelines, SES AI pivoting away from automotive EV cells, GM exiting its Indiana JV and the SES Chungju venture, Honda canceling its North American EV launches before partnering with QuantumScape [88][99][60][101][102][7].

## Scale-up reality: pilot lines, GWh, costs, manufacturing challenges

### Announced pilot lines / capacities (sourced numbers only)
- **QuantumScape Eagle Line** — automated pilot line at San Jose headquarters, inaugurated Feb 4, 2026; no GWh figure published; cells for OEM sampling and field testing; licensing model means VW/PowerCo does scale manufacturing [2][11][12].
- **Solid Power** — continuous sulfide-electrolyte pilot line: factory acceptance testing of all key equipment complete, commissioning targeted end 2026; SK On cell line in Korea (SAT complete April 2026) and BMW line in Germany — "cell production lines using our technology on three continents" (CEO John Van Scoter) [13][14].
- **Samsung SDI** — S-line pilot Suwon (6,500 m², since 2022); Ulsan mass-production line planned for H2 2027; 25T KRW (~$17B) 2026–2040 investment across Ulsan/Cheonan [19][23][123][124].
- **SK On** — Daejeon pilot plant 4,628 m² (completed Sept 2025); commercialization 2029 [33][35].
- **Toyota/Idemitsu** — large electrolyte pilot plant (FID Jan 2026; completion end 2027); Idemitsu Chiba lithium-sulfide plant 1,000 t/yr; METI-certified production plan [24][28][29][30].
- **Gotion** — 0.2 GWh all-solid pilot (yield >90%) → 2 GWh line design complete; materials plan 50,000 t Li2S + 100,000 t electrolyte by 2030 [71][72][75].
- **ProLogium** — Taoyuan gigafactory (operating 2024, >600,000 cells shipped); Dunkirk phase 1 0.8 GWh by 2028 [64][65][66].
- **WeLion** — ~28.2 GWh claimed total capacity (semi-solid) across four provinces [87].
- **Nissan** — Yokohama pilot line (Jan 2025); FY2028 launch [91][94].
- **BYD** — Shenzhen pilot line; ~1,000 demo vehicles in 2027 [86].
- **CATL** — small-batch all-solid production targeted 2027 [83][85].
- **China-wide (context):** reported planned solid-state capacity 345.7 GWh (2025) and 390.7 GWh (2027) per GACO report (industry estimate) [109]; SMM reports a wave of 30 GWh-class projects and a first national SSB technical standard due July 2026 [127][78].

### Cost reality (sourced estimates; wide disagreement — see Forecasts section)
- **S&P Global Mobility:** SSB costs ~$500/kWh by 2025, over 5× lithium-ion; initial use limited to premium segments [112].
- **CRU:** ASSB production cost at best 2.3× conventional Li-ion cells today; cost parity "will not be achieved in the next decade" [113].
- **TrendForce:** solid-state costs expected to fall to CNY 0.6–0.7/Wh only by 2035 [111].
- **Fastmarkets:** LFP cells at $54.63/kWh in China (April 2026, +13.6% y/y); proposes $85/kWh as proof-of-concept benchmark for solid-state scalability [114].
- **BYD:** targets cost parity with liquid Li-ion at ~$70/kWh (its own stated goal) [86].
- **Gotion:** targets 1 yuan/Wh for Gemstone [76].
- **WardsAuto citing industry:** solid-state cells currently 10–30× more expensive than conventional Li-ion [58].
- **Gotion + Factorial claims vs. reality check:** semi-solid G-Yuan is already GWh-scale in deployment per SMM [128].

### Manufacturing challenges (sourced)
- **Sulfide electrolytes** are moisture-sensitive → dry-room requirements dominate plant design (Solid Power's own pilot construction; IOPscience review on ASSB fabrication) [14][115].
- **Ceramic separators** need high-temperature sintering/heat treatment — QuantumScape's Cobra is explicitly a next-generation heat-treatment process [10].
- **Solid–solid interfacial contact, mechanical integrity, large-scale manufacturability** are the three hardest ASSB challenges; dry-electrode processing is a key enabler for sulfide systems (IOPscience review; LG; Nissan–LiCAP; Springer dry-electrode review) [38][91][115][116].
- **Thin lithium metal anodes** are a cost bottleneck (Nature Energy techno-economic assessment) [117].
- **Process simplification:** ProLogium claims core production reduced from 17 to 11 steps and "hot-flow dehydration" of 8 min vs 8 hr (self-reported, CEO interview) [131].
- Academic cost modeling shows sulfide ASSBs can approach competitiveness only if material-compatibility issues are solved and production is scaled (6 GWh scenario modeled) [116].

## Semi-solid vs. full solid-state — honesty of claims

- **Factorial FEST is quasi-solid**, not full solid-state: company's own materials say "quasi-solid electrolyte technology" — a solid matrix infused with liquid/gel-like electrolyte. Industry analyses (Electronic Design; MotorTrend) call the Mercedes EQS prototype and Stellantis Charger Daytona cells semi-solid/quasi-solid [48][53][57][125][133]. The "first solid-state EV" headlines around the EQS should be read as first quasi-solid lithium-metal road car, not full ASSB.
- **CATL "condensed battery" is a semi-solid product** — CATL's own chief scientist called it a type of semi-solid state product with condensed electrolyte; Prof. Fichtner (Helmholtz-Institut Ulm) classifies it as an "almost solid-state battery" [80][118].
- **NIO/WeLion 150 kWh is semi-solid** (gel-like polymer/oxide+polymer composite, "in-situ solidification"); NIO never claimed full solid-state [88][90].
- **Gotion G-Yuan is quasi-solid/semi-solid**, positioned as a bridge to the Gemstone all-solid line [77][128].
- **SES AI cells are semi-solid** (hybrid solid-liquid) lithium-metal [61].
- **Full solid-state claims (defensible as of mid-2026):** Solid Power (sulfide, but with LiSi anode in commercial target), Toyota/Idemitsu (sulfide), Samsung SDI (anode-less oxide-type), ProLogium (all-inorganic ceramic), Nissan (sulfide), CATL/BYD/Gotion all-solid programs (2027+), LG (sulfide R&D), Blue Solutions (polymer LMP — genuinely liquid-free, but polymer-based with operating-temperature constraints) [14][19][25][44][64][82][86][91][118].
- **QuantumScape nuance:** the separator is a solid ceramic and the cell is anode-free lithium metal, but the industry debates whether the presence of liquid in the cathode makes it "hybrid" — academic literature groups such designs under "hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte systems"; QuantumScape itself markets the QSE-5 as solid-state lithium-metal [1][9][119][120]. Flag: terminology contested; QS's own marketing calls it solid-state.
- **Bottom line:** as of mid-2026 every mass-produced "solid-state" automotive product on the road or in series production (NIO/WeLion, CATL condensed, Factorial-based prototypes) is semi-solid/quasi-solid. All-full-solid products target 2027–2030 [86][88][110][120][128].

- **IDTechEx:** "Solid-State Batteries 2026–2036" report — SSB market could reach **US$10B by 2036** [103]; earlier editions projected $9B by 2035 and $8B by 2031 — i.e., IDTechEx keeps pushing its market-size horizon outward as dates slip [104][105][106].
- **CICC (China Intl Capital):** global solid-state shipments **808 GWh in 2030**, of which semi-solid >650 GWh (power 466 GWh, ESS 90 GWh, eVTOL 60 GWh, consumer 36 GWh) [107].
- **CITIC Securities (via ETN news):** global penetration 1.7% (2025) → 8.4% (2030); capacity 38 GWh (2025) → 509 GWh (2030) [108].
- **GACO (China report):** China planned capacity 345.7 GWh (2025) → 390.7 GWh (2027); shipments to reach 70 GWh by 2030 [109].
- **Benchmark Mineral Intelligence:** consensus framing that 2027 = demonstration year for SSB EVs, large-scale production by 2030 [110].
- **Meridian Consensus (aggregator):** $1.2B (2025) → $18.1B (2036) at 28% CAGR, sulfide 42% share — **low-quality source, treat as indicative only** (not in evidence table beyond this note).
- **BNEF:** no accessible dedicated solid-state adoption forecast found in this research pass (BNEF hits were energy-storage-market forecasts). **Gap — flagged.** 
- **Disagreements worth flagging:** (a) IDTechEx's rolling horizon vs. CICC's aggressive 808 GWh-by-2030; (b) CRU's "no cost parity this decade" vs. BYD's self-stated $70/kWh parity goal; (c) TrendForce's CNY 0.6–0.7/Wh by 2035 vs. Gotion's 1 yuan/Wh target; (d) CITIC's 509 GWh (2030) vs. CICC's 808 GWh (2030) — a ~60% gap between two Chinese broker forecasts.

## Executive summary (inference-led synthesis)

- **No company has yet shipped a commercial full-solid-state automotive battery.** As of mid-2026 the landscape is: pilot lines up, B-sample cells shipping to OEMs, one OEM road-test prototype (Mercedes EQS with Factorial quasi-solid cells, Feb 2025), one North American road-test vehicle (Stellantis Dodge Charger Daytona with Factorial, June 2026), and Chinese semi-solid packs (NIO/WeLion) that were mass-produced then discontinued for lack of demand [87][88][50][52].
- **Electrolyte routes are split three ways:** sulfide (Toyota/Idemitsu, Solid Power, SK On via Solid Power, LG, CATL all-solid, BYD, Gotion Gemstone, Nissan, Hyundai), oxide ceramic (Samsung SDI, QuantumScape's ceramic separator, ProLogium), and polymer (Blue Solutions) — plus quasi-solid/semi-solid polymer-gel hybrids (Factorial FEST, CATL condensed, WeLion, Gotion G-Yuan, SES AI) [14][19][48][79][90][44][127].
- **Claimed launch years cluster 2027–2030:** Toyota 2027–2028 [28], Samsung SDI H2 2027 [23], Nissan FY2028 [93][94], SK On 2029 [33][34], CATL/BYD small-batch 2027 [85], Gotion mass production 2030 [72], Mercedes "by end of decade" [49], Hyundai/Kia publicly skeptical ("not before 2030") [99][100].
- **The single most honest market signal:** several 2025–2026 reversals — NIO halting its 150 kWh semi-solid pack, Hyundai/Kia publicly walking back timelines, SES AI pivoting away from automotive EV cells, GM exiting its Indiana JV and the SES Chungju venture, Honda canceling its North American EV launches before partnering with QuantumScape [88][99][60][101][102][7].

## Scale-up reality: pilot lines, GWh, costs, manufacturing challenges

### Announced pilot lines / capacities (sourced numbers only)
- **QuantumScape Eagle Line** — automated pilot line at San Jose headquarters, inaugurated Feb 4, 2026; no GWh figure published; cells for OEM sampling and field testing; licensing model means VW/PowerCo does scale manufacturing [2][11][12].
- **Solid Power** — continuous sulfide-electrolyte pilot line: factory acceptance testing of all key equipment complete, commissioning targeted end 2026; SK On cell line in Korea (SAT complete April 2026) and BMW line in Germany — "cell production lines using our technology on three continents" (CEO John Van Scoter) [13][14].

- **SK On** — Daejeon pilot plant 4,628 m² (completed Sept 2025); commercialization 2029 [33][35].
- **Toyota/Idemitsu** — large electrolyte pilot plant (FID Jan 2026; completion end 2027); Idemitsu Chiba lithium-sulfide plant 1,000 t/yr; METI-certified production plan [24][28][29][30].
- **Gotion** — 0.2 GWh all-solid pilot (yield >90%) → 2 GWh line design complete; materials plan 50,000 t Li2S + 100,000 t electrolyte by 2030 [71][72][75].

- **Nissan** — Yokohama pilot line (Jan 2025); FY2028 launch [91][94].
- **BYD** — Shenzhen pilot line; ~1,000 demo vehicles in 2027 [86].
- **CATL** — small-batch all-solid production targeted 2027 [83][85].
- **China-wide (context):** reported planned solid-state capacity 345.7 GWh (2025) and 390.7 GWh (2027) per GACO report (industry estimate) [109]; SMM reports a wave of 30 GWh-class projects and a first national SSB technical standard due July 2026 [127][78].

### Cost reality (sourced estimates; wide disagreement — see Forecasts section)
- **S&P Global Mobility:** SSB costs ~$500/kWh by 2025, over 5× lithium-ion; initial use limited to premium segments [112].
- **CRU:** ASSB production cost at best 2.3× conventional Li-ion cells today; cost parity "will not be achieved in the next decade" [113].
- **TrendForce:** solid-state costs expected to fall to CNY 0.6–0.7/Wh only by 2035 [111].
- **Fastmarkets:** LFP cells at $54.63/kWh in China (April 2026, +13.6% y/y); proposes $85/kWh as proof-of-concept benchmark for solid-state scalability [114].
- **BYD:** targets cost parity with liquid Li-ion at ~$70/kWh (its own stated goal) [86].
- **Gotion:** targets 1 yuan/Wh for Gemstone [76].
- **WardsAuto citing industry:** solid-state cells currently 10–30× more expensive than conventional Li-ion [58].
- **Gotion + Factorial claims vs. reality check:** semi-solid G-Yuan is already GWh-scale in deployment per SMM [128].

### Manufacturing challenges (sourced)
- **Sulfide electrolytes** are moisture-sensitive → dry-room requirements dominate plant design (Solid Power's own pilot construction; IOPscience review on ASSB fabrication) [14][115].
- **Ceramic separators** need high-temperature sintering/heat treatment — QuantumScape's Cobra is explicitly a next-generation heat-treatment process [10].
- **Solid–solid interfacial contact, mechanical integrity, large-scale manufacturability** are the three hardest ASSB challenges; dry-electrode processing is a key enabler for sulfide systems (IOPscience review; LG; Nissan–LiCAP; Springer dry-electrode review) [38][91][115][116].
- **Thin lithium metal anodes** are a cost bottleneck (Nature Energy techno-economic assessment) [117].
- **Process simplification:** ProLogium claims core production reduced from 17 to 11 steps and "hot-flow dehydration" of 8 min vs 8 hr (self-reported, CEO interview) [131].
- Academic cost modeling shows sulfide ASSBs can approach competitiveness only if material-compatibility issues are solved and production is scaled (6 GWh scenario modeled) [116].

## Semi-solid vs. full solid-state — honesty of claims

- **Factorial FEST is quasi-solid**, not full solid-state: company's own materials say "quasi-solid electrolyte technology" — a solid matrix infused with liquid/gel-like electrolyte. Industry analyses (Electronic Design; MotorTrend) call the Mercedes EQS prototype and Stellantis Charger Daytona cells semi-solid/quasi-solid [48][53][57][125][133]. The "first solid-state EV" headlines around the EQS should be read as first quasi-solid lithium-metal road car, not full ASSB.
- **CATL "condensed battery" is a semi-solid product** — CATL's own chief scientist called it a type of semi-solid state product with condensed electrolyte; Prof. Fichtner (Helmholtz-Institut Ulm) classifies it as an "almost solid-state battery" [80][118].
- **NIO/WeLion 150 kWh is semi-solid** (gel-like polymer/oxide+polymer composite, "in-situ solidification"); NIO never claimed full solid-state [88][90].
- **Gotion G-Yuan is quasi-solid/semi-solid**, positioned as a bridge to the Gemstone all-solid line [77][128].
- **SES AI cells are semi-solid** (hybrid solid-liquid) lithium-metal [61].
- **Full solid-state claims (defensible as of mid-2026):** Solid Power (sulfide, but with LiSi anode in commercial target), Toyota/Idemitsu (sulfide), Samsung SDI (anode-less oxide-type), ProLogium (all-inorganic ceramic), Nissan (sulfide), CATL/BYD/Gotion all-solid programs (2027+), LG (sulfide R&D), Blue Solutions (polymer LMP — genuinely liquid-free, but polymer-based with operating-temperature constraints) [14][19][25][44][64][82][86][91][118].
- **QuantumScape nuance:** the separator is a solid ceramic and the cell is anode-free lithium metal, but the industry debates whether the presence of liquid in the cathode makes it "hybrid" — academic literature groups such designs under "hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte systems"; QuantumScape itself markets the QSE-5 as solid-state lithium-metal [1][9][119][120]. Flag: terminology contested; QS's own marketing calls it solid-state.
- **Bottom line:** as of mid-2026 every mass-produced "solid-state" automotive product on the road or in series production (NIO/WeLion, CATL condensed, Factorial-based prototypes) is semi-solid/quasi-solid. All-full-solid products target 2027–2030 [86][88][110][120][128].
